messages:
olivia: Quick sync — thinking about a small RFC follow-up: can we compact span payloads at ingest to save storage and egress cost? tradeoffs re: evals and attribution.
kevin: Interested. Do you mean trimming non-essential attrs or collapsing repeated child spans?
olivia: Both. Proposal: upstream drop high-cardinality debug fields and collapse synthetic internal retries into a single span with a count field. Keep full payload for sampled traces.
sam: Sounds reasonable. Main risk is losing signal for root-cause analysis and evals that replay full traces. How often do we need full fidelity?
natalie: For cost attribution we need some stable keys: billing_key, tenant_id, route. Those must survive compaction. Anything else can be optional.
devin: Another risk: downstream correlators (rerank, QA evals) expect verbatim span names/attrs. If we change shape, they may break. Need a compatibility layer or schema-version.
kevin: Could we attach a lightweight manifest per compacted trace that indicates what was removed and where to request full payloads from cold storage? e.g., manifest -> s3://trace-archive/<id>.
olivia: That was my thought. Compacting keeps hot-path small but manifest points to archival bucket. Only sampled pulls full trace.
sam: Operational questions: compaction at edge vs ingest-service? Doing it at edge reduces network egress but complicates SDKs. Ingest-service centralizes logic but we've already paid egress.
kevin: Prefer central ingest for correctness and easier rollout. Edge compaction could be opt-in later.
natalie: For billing we must not change billing_key computation. Also ensure compaction doesn't remove tags used by cost rules (e.g., feature_flag=on).
devin: Wire a schema version header: `obsv_schema_version: 2` when compacted. Downstreams can reject or backfill if they need full.
olivia: Proposed minimal compact spec: remove `debug.*`, `profiler.*`, drop `stackframes` beyond top-1, collapse retries into `retry_count`, keep `attrs.{billing_key, tenant_id, route}`. Example: ```json
{
  "span_id": "...",
  "name": "http.request",
  "retry_count": 3,
  "attrs": {"billing_key":"bk_123","tenant_id":"t_51","route":"/generate"},
  "manifest": "s3://trace-archive/2360012345_full.json"
}
```
sam: Looks good. Can you add TTL on manifests (90d) and a cheap index for manifest lookup by trace id?
kevin: Also add a flag for "full_capture_required" on tenant configs (enterprise customers can opt out of compaction).
natalie: Important: update our cost attribution pipeline to operate on compacted shape — i.e., prefer attrs.* first, fallback to manifest hydrations only for missing keys. Avoid hydrating for billing at query time.
devin: Agree. Implement hydration as async job for analytics/evals only. Don't block billing.
olivia: Rollout plan idea: feature gate behind `compact_spans` per dataset, start 10% of traffic next week, 50% after 2 weeks, and full after infra metrics look stable.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: compact-spans-v1 -> canary on ingest-service 2026-03-25T08:00Z
kevin: Metrics to watch: ingest CPU, peak egress bytes, manifest write latency, billing key missing-rate (<0.01% target), and downstream errors from evaluators.
sam: One more: add an end-to-end test that rehydrates a manifest and runs one of our eval suites to ensure parity.
natalie: I'll update the cost-rule docs and add a migration note for partners.
olivia: Thanks all — I'll draft a short RFC PR summarizing this and include sample code + rollout timeline. Ping me if you want to be a reviewer. :thumbsup:
